races.title: State Assembly, District 13
races.note: The top two finishers from the Nov 3, 2026 count. Everyone else in this race is coming.

cands.name: Rhodesia Ransom
cands.bio: Democrat and incumbent Assemblymember for District 13 (San Joaquin County) since December 2024. Previously on the Tracy Planning Commission (2009-2016) and Tracy City Council (2016-2020). Served as district director for Rep. Josh Harder from 2021. Nonprofit co-founder and business owner.

endorsements.text: 2026 endorsements listed by Ballotpedia include the Democratic Party of California, California Federation of Labor Unions, California Teachers Association, California Nurses Association, IUOE Local 3, National Union of Healthcare Workers, and Equality California.
Her campaign site says she has been endorsed by the San Joaquin County Deputy Sheriff's Association, San Joaquin County Corrections Officers Association, and Manteca Police Officers Association.

cands.gaps: We could not find her birthplace or the year she moved to the San Joaquin area. The pages reviewed list no bills she has sponsored and show no actions on data centers, homestead property taxes, investor or foreign land buying, growth limits, immigration enforcement, guns, abortion, or school choice. We found no stated positions from her on data centers or on development, and no documented controversies.

local.label: Roots 90: Wikipedia says she grew up in San Francisco and attended San Francisco State University; her birthplace is not stated in the pages reviewed, and she has since lived in San Joaquin County, where she raised three children.

score.why: Raised $0, under $5,000 for this office: too little money to score fairly.

qual.background: Assemblymember since 2024; Tracy City Council 2016-2020; Tracy Planning Commission 2009-2016; district director for Rep. Josh Harder from April 2021; nonprofit co-founder and business owner; master's degree in public administration; says she has taught graduate public policy and public finance courses.
qual.why: She has held legislative office at the state and city level and has worked in policy and as a congressional staff director, which places her in the high range. Her teaching claim comes only from her campaign site.

cands.name: Tom Patti
cands.bio: Republican candidate for Assembly District 13. Stockton business owner (Delta Cranes, a crane company he built with his father) and former amateur boxer. Served on the San Joaquin County Board of Supervisors, District 3, from 2017 to January 2025, including a term as chair. Ran for Congress in 2022 and Stockton mayor in 2024.

endorsements.text: 2026 Assembly race: Republican Party of California, San Joaquin County Republican Party, and Reform California (among others listed by Ballotpedia).
2024 Stockton mayor race (per his own survey): Stockton Police Officers Association, Deputy Sheriffs Association, Police Officers Research Association of California, and Stockton Business Alliance.

cands.gaps: We could not confirm Tom Patti's birthplace: Ballotpedia says Stockton and Wikipedia says New York, and we left it blank. We found no 2026 Assembly campaign platform or questionnaire, so we have no stated positions from him on data centers, property taxes, foreign or investor land buying, H-1B or immigration, guns, abortion, or school choice for this race. We found no documented actions in office on those topics from pages we could read, so the "did" list is empty. His claim that he raised sheriff's deputy pay comes only from his own survey. We found no news reporting on controversies and no documented foreign ties. We did not find his age or exact date of birth, or when he first came to California as a child.

local.label: Roots 90: He says he is a second-generation Stocktonian who attended local schools and Delta College, and he has lived in San Joaquin County as an adult since returning in 2001, but sources conflict on his birthplace (Stockton vs. New York), so the raised-here score applies.

land.label: 1 documented position for data centers or more development

score.why: Raised $0, under $5,000 for this office: too little money to score fairly.

qual.background: Two-term San Joaquin County supervisor (2017–2025) who served as board chair, and a second-generation business owner (Delta Cranes). He has no state legislative service on record.
qual.why: Local elected office with county budget responsibilities and business ownership put him in the middle band; he has no prior legislative service or formal law, policy or budget career.
qual.label: Local elected office with county budget responsibilities and business ownership put him in the middle band; he has no prior legislative service or formal law, policy or budget career.

back-police-order.evidence: In his 2024 Ballotpedia survey for Stockton mayor, he said he would push to rebuild the Police Department, pay officers a fair wage, restore neighborhood police stations and crack down on criminals. He also said that as supervisor he reopened the Deputy Sheriffs' contract and raised pay to the median (his own account, not independently verified).

land_positions.quote_or_summary: In his 2024 Stockton mayoral survey he said of housing, "We need more quality, more quantity, and more affordable options," and said he would push for redevelopment of downtown into entertainment districts. He also described his vision as "smart economic growth with an eye on the future of sustainable communities."
